observations: body L1, L20, L43-L44: «Al–Battānī» (L1, L20) and «al–Battānī» (L43) are letter-spaced, with long dashes (5.4, 5.5 and 5.2 pt), and so is «al–Khāzinī» (L44, 6.2 pt); the dashes of «6–24» (L1) and of «az–zīǵ», «as–sanǵarī» and «80,r.–81,r.» (L44) measure 5.4, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.3 pt.
body L2: the m of «10ᵐ», the minutes of time, is a raised italic m; a speck stands before the 1. One sixth of an hour is 10 minutes of time.
body L6, L23: the minus signs print as bars 9.5 and 9.4 pt long, like dashes; they are set as minus signs.
body L8, L13: a speck stands before the guillemet that opens «praecessione Lunae» (L8); specks stand over the n of «in» (L13).
body L10, L17, L19, L42, L46: the dashes measure 10.1, 10.0, 10.1 and 9.5 pt; the dash before «Dicit» (L46) prints in two pieces, 2.5 and 6.0 pt, 9.2 pt over all.
body L14-L18: each run of dots has five dots.

body L20-L27: the rule described, to take ⅙ hour from ϑ + ε² when the Moon lies between the ascendant and the nonagesimal and to add it when the Moon lies beyond the nonagesimal, so that the auxiliary parallax is always the greater, is al-Battānī's rule for a third parallax greater than the second (translation, p. 105, l. 7–13, with l. 18–19). The lines cited, p. 105, l. 27–33, give the reverse rule for a third parallax smaller than the second: ⅙ hour added when the Moon is less than 90° from the ascendant and taken away when it is more, and the auxiliary parallax there is the smaller (l. 31). The second 3 of «33» (L22) prints broken.

body L33: as on p. 277, L40-L41, the first parallax is divided here by the praecessio Lunae; al-Battānī's text divides it by the hourly motion of the Moon (translation, p. 104, l. 21–22; p. 110, l. 11–12).
body L40: «motus aequatus» is in roman here, in italics in L9 and L19, as printed.
body L42: the 2 of «ε²» prints deformed; a heavy bracket closes the addition begun on p. 277, L4.
